findings.title: Single-term fragments are returned without parentheses, so top-level OR can escape composition
findings.description: `getBaseConditions()` wraps each side in parentheses only when both auth and filter exist (line 73). Otherwise it returns the one fragment as-is (lines 74-77). Several fragments are themselves a top-level `OR`: the org and team authorization builders (lines 171-174 and 204-207) and the `eventTypeId` filter (lines 105-107). Prisma's `sql` tag inlines nested fragments without adding parentheses. A caller that writes `WHERE "status" = 'accepted' AND ${baseConditions}` for org scope with members gets `("status"='accepted' AND teamBranch) OR userBranch`, so user-branch rows ignore the caller's predicate. That is an authorization-scope leak if a tenant or visibility predicate is added this way. Nothing in the repo composes the fragment yet. The only use is the sole-predicate test at `packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:481-484`, and several assertions lock in the unwrapped form. Suggested fix: wrap every returned fragment in parentheses. One `joinSql(terms, "AND" | "OR")` helper that wraps each term would also replace the four duplicated `reduce` blocks (lines 73, 119-122, 171-174, 204-207). Add a DB-backed test that composes the base condition with an extra predicate.

findings.title: Caching tests were deleted, leaving the cache path untested
findings.description: The diff removes the `describe("Caching")` block with "should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions". The caching code is still there (`insightsBooking.ts:83-95`), so nothing covers it now. The sibling `insightsRouting.integration-test.ts:444-500` still has equivalent Caching tests, so the two suites diverge. The removed assertions only needed the new `Prisma.sql` expectation. The `=== undefined` check at line 91 matters because `null` is a cached value. A truthiness check would silently break that case, and the removed tests were the guard for it. Restore both tests with updated expectations.

findings.title: Loosened constructor type lets invalid scope/teamId combinations compile and silently return no rows
findings.description: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` replaces the discriminated union as the constructor input (line 58). It has `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` and `teamId?: number`. That means `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` with no `teamId` now type-checks. At runtime `safeParse` fails (lines 62-63), `this.options` becomes `null`, and every condition collapses to `1=0`. Failing closed is the right security default, but it is silent: there is no log, and a caller bug shows up as empty results instead of a compile error. Suggested fix: type the input as `z.input<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>`. That keeps the union's compile-time checks and removes the hand-copied shape. If untrusted input must pass through, log the `safeParse` error at the boundary.

findings.title: Some branches in `getBaseConditions` cannot run
findings.description: `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `Promise<Prisma.Sql>`, and every path of `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns a `Sql` object. Objects are always truthy, so `else if (filterConditions)` (line 76) and the final `else` returning `NOTHING_CONDITION` (lines 78-79) are unreachable. The code is still correct, since a "no auth" result is already `1=0`, but it implies auth can be absent. Either remove those branches or make the auth result nullable so the "no auth" path is explicit.

findings.title: Tests assert exact SQL text, which locks in the unwrapped OR structure
findings.description: Most auth and filter tests compare with `toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)`, including lines 295-299 and 332-343. These pin whitespace, operand order, and parenthesization. They would still pass if the composed SQL were wrong in the way described in the first finding. The earlier suite asserted Prisma `where` objects, so this is the same implementation-level style, not new debt. The one DB-backed test of `getBaseConditions` (lines 480-491) checks behavior, but only for the auth-plus-filter path. Add DB-backed cases for auth-only and for a composed predicate.

findings.title: The sibling `insightsRouting` service still uses the Prisma `where` shape
findings.description: `InsightsBookingService` now returns raw `Prisma.Sql`. `InsightsRoutingService` still returns `Prisma.RoutingFormResponseDenormalizedWhereInput` (`insightsRouting.ts:78-92`) and still has its caching tests. The two services share a structure but now build queries differently. That may be deliberate, since the booking query runs against a view, but nothing in the diff documents it. If it is deliberate, add a comment on the service explaining why. Otherwise plan to align them.

findings.title: Filter and authorization values are bound parameters
findings.description: User-influenced values (`eventTypeId`, `memberUserId`, and IDs from the org and team lookups) all go through `Prisma.sql` interpolation and become bound parameters. Arrays are passed as single parameters with `= ANY(...)`. Column names are fixed literals. The changed code has no string concatenation and no `$queryRawUnsafe`. Injection risk lies in how callers execute the fragment, not in this file.

findings.title: SQL identifiers match the view, and the translation is equivalent
findings.description: The column names used (`"userId"`, `"teamId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"`) match `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1682-1708`, which has no `@map` attributes. The migration `20250505135207_create_booking_time_status_denormalized` defines the view with the same columns. `teamId: null` maps to `IS NULL`. The `in: []` cases are covered by the length guards at lines 166 and 200. The `1=0` NOTHING condition is equivalent to the old `{ id: -1 }` for positive IDs. The removed `findMany` has no callers in the repo; a search found only the service and its test.

Tests assert exact SQL text, which locks in the unwrapped OR structure
